learning_objective: 🎯 Learn how psychologists define abnormal behavior, explore classification systems like DSM-5 and ICD, and examine major psychological disorders!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Abnormal behavior is typically defined using the 'Four Ds': Deviance (violating social norms), Distress (causing personal suffering), Dysfunction (impairing daily functioning), and Danger (risk to self or others).

To diagnose and study disorders systematically, mental health professionals use global manuals like the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders (DSM-5) and the International Classification of Diseases (ICD).

Disorders are categorized into groups: Anxiety Disorders (generalized anxiety, panic, phobias), Depressive & Bipolar Disorders (mood swings, extreme sadness), Schizophrenia (hallucinations, delusions), Somatoform Disorders (physical symptoms without organic cause), and Dissociative Disorders (identity confusion).

Disorders arise from a combination of biological factors (genetics, chemical imbalances), psychological factors (trauma, faulty thinking), and sociocultural factors (stress, poverty, cultural expectations), often explained by the Biopsychosocial model.

fun_activity.title: 🚫 Debunking Mental Health Myths
fun_activity.instructions: List three common stereotypes or myths people hold about mental illness (e.g., 'people with mental illness are violent'). Research facts to debunk each myth. Promoting awareness helps reduce social stigma!

exam_tips: 📌 Memorize the 'Four Ds' of abnormality (Deviance, Distress, Dysfunction, Danger)—frequently asked in 1 or 2-mark questions.
📌 Know the distinction between Obsessions (repetitive thoughts) and Compulsions (repetitive behaviors) in OCD.
📌 Briefly understand positive and negative symptoms of Schizophrenia (e.g., hallucinations vs. flattened affect).
quick_recap: ⭐ Abnormality is evaluated based on deviance, distress, dysfunction, and danger.
⭐ Manuals like DSM-5 and ICD provide standardized diagnostic criteria for mental health professionals.
⭐ Disorders span anxiety, mood, psychotic, and somatic conditions influenced by biological and social factors.
